mainText:
If you only remember one thing: the people who write A I safety reports are now leaving the labs, and saying why out loud.

Number one. Open A I's safety lead quits. From your Rundown and That One A I. David Robinson oversaw safety reports for twelve frontier launches. He also drafted Open A I's Preparedness Framework. He left after three and a half years. His essay in The Atlantic calls the culture broken. He says labs should run like nuclear plants, with layers of backup. This follows Open A I firing three researchers who reportedly shared sensitive information with an outside safety group. Why it matters: the alarm is coming from inside the building, which makes it harder to wave away.

Number two. Agents hit platform limits. From That One A I. Apple is tightening Full Disk Access on Mac, partly because of A I agents. This follows a report about Meta's Muse Mac app, and a flaw in Chat G P T's Mac app. Meta also open sourced tools so developers can build hardware that connects to Muse. And Anthropic released mods for Claude Code on October first. They can block risky commands before they run. Why it matters: agents need deep access to be useful, and platform owners are starting to say no.

Number three. China, chips and geopolitics. From your China A I Weekly Digest. Deep Seek open sourced software tools for Huawei's Ascend chips. The aim is to loosen Nvidia's grip. The U S and China agreed an A I incident hotline at the Xi and Trump summit. Days later, Trump rejected working with China on A I safety. The Information reports Beijing may let Alibaba and ByteDance buy new Nvidia chips. A senior House Democrat is asking whether U S export controls are actually working. And China widened travel limits to the families of top A I researchers. Why it matters: chips, talent and safety diplomacy are now one tangled story.

Number four. Money and models. Manus relaunched as Manus two point oh, with an always on agent called Cue. The reported valuation is four billion dollars. Deep Seek raised about seven billion dollars, and doubled revenue to about one billion, ahead of a planned I P O. China's generative A I users passed seven hundred million. Why it matters: the personal agent race is the defining battleground, in both countries.

Number five. Good news, and also in your reads. The Rundown's staff describe agents booking D M V appointments and planning trips. Small errands, handled. Also in your reads, The New Yorker covers the battle to pass a wealth tax, and the New York Film Festival. Your Readwise saves were unavailable today. Why it matters: the small errand agent is the version most people will actually feel.

The thread today: safety talent leaving, platforms pushing back, and a chip race splitting in two. That's your briefing. Have a good one.
